feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and could be sharper with more quantified outcomes and less overlap across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization support trust and show increasing responsibility.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines communications leadership with Drupal, analytics, workflow design, and multimedia execution.  
- Good clarity and structure in experience bullets, with several concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers).

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics beyond scope: include outcomes such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, production savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap; consolidating would improve focus and save space.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other serial lists); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the experience section, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it with sharper phrasing and one or two concrete differentiators would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with more specific, evidence-backed positioning tied to enterprise web, governance, and advocacy communications.
- Add one clearer seniority signal, e.g., “leading digital strategy and operations” for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “workflows and systems” overlap with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording elsewhere.
- “Advocacy messaging” is echoed in Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/operational capabilities will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more specific, senior-level phrasing: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Align style and parallel structure across items; use noun phrases consistently.
- Consider this version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS & web platform administration • Editorial workflow & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, prioritize the most distinctive strengths: governance, platform modernization, analytics, and systems/workflow design.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills/Technical + IT, especially web/CMS, analytics, workflow systems, and multimedia.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a broad responsibility list. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or deliverables to distinguish it from your prior NACo leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel communications systems.”
- Combine overlapping systems/governance bullets: merge digital systems, workflows, analytics, and best practices into one outcome-focused bullet.
- Make deliverables concrete: name launched microsites, toolkit hubs, search prototypes, workflow redesigns, or platform enhancements; add metrics if possible.
- Rephrase for impact, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member resource hubs.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Improved web operations through CMS development, front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and governance recommendations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; emphasize consultant-specific projects and advisory scope instead.
- Microsite and AI search details also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-led.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based; add performance if available (open rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume) rather than “reaching tens of thousands.”
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: built first in-house studio; expanded analytics stack (GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery); formalized governance and publishing standards.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; differentiate this entry by emphasizing enterprise ownership, modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video-program language overlaps with older NACo roles; focus here on building organizational production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level: editorial operations, newsletter scale, and launch of recurring advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across NACo.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is repeated in adjacent NACo roles; vary wording to stress operations/process ownership here.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and governance strengths rather than broad communications wording.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-seniority language tied to recent work.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex organizations
- Public-sector digital communications and advocacy campaigns
- Audience-centered content strategy and information architecture
- If space allows, use “mission-driven organizations” instead of “complex organizations” to align with the header.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim; consider differentiating this section by framing around leadership scope rather than repeating capability labels.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is weaker than the experience bullets; “digital communications and advocacy campaigns” better matches the CV’s evidence.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages

- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths tied to Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most relevant/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations.
- Consider dropping lower-signal or less evidenced platforms here (e.g., WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) unless they are important for target roles.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search and discovery design.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, then list key platforms.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Livestreaming

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo experience bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope, production environment, and leadership-level capability rather than generic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as tighter, higher-signal phrases: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to align with the in-house studio achievement.
- Replace “Livestreaming” with “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” to sound more outcome-oriented and senior.
- If accurate, add scale or complexity: “multi-camera,” “recurring advocacy programming,” or “end-to-end studio operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and video/livestream work are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this section should stay concise and specialized.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to emphasize current, relevant platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, demonstrated platforms first: **Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to actual use: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector sites) • SharePoint (intranets/content management) • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to sharpen scope: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- Keep it platform-only; avoid mixing in modernization or implementation language already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one more concise.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating extra Drupal detail here unless other platforms also get context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use and modernize outdated phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Replace with a tighter list: **HTML • CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; it can date the profile.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “used for Drupal front-end builds, analytics deployment, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if you want this section to stay tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more intentional by separating automation builders from collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strategic relevance: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases)** • **Power Automate / Zapier (process automation)** • **Jira / Asana / Trello (project workflows)**
- Consider trimming one or two lower-value collaboration tools if not used recently; keep the strongest, most current systems tied to enterprise workflow design.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating those exact phrases elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams/Basecamp/Trello are lower-impact than automation platforms and may dilute the leadership/technical positioning if overemphasized.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and audience engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign setup, segmentation, automation, newsletter operations)**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: **enterprise/member communications**, **journey orchestration**, or **audience segmentation**
- Keep only platforms you can credibly discuss in interviews; if one was lightly used, move it later in the list or remove it

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with multiple recent NACo bullets about newsletters and digital channel leadership; avoid adding generic “email marketing” language elsewhere
- “Engagement” is vague unless supported—use terms like **segmentation**, **automation**, or **member communications** instead

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website traffic supported, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, email/social volume, or size of team supervised.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic claims like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specific actions such as “standardized publishing workflows” or “supported website refresh.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and coordinated day-to-day content execution across web, email, social and multimedia. Provided direct guidance to a digital media associate and helped formalize early publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the media work concise.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and distinct contribution: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the media sentence and make the podcast the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a clearer outcome if available: e.g., “produced multimedia content to translate research and policy work into member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, series length, audiences supported, or programs/policy initiatives served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media roles; keep this item more focused on research/innovation support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad “digital communications” language here since stronger, more recent entries already cover that.
